        "\n",
        "# pandas handles our dataset as a structured table (like Excel in Python)\n",
        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "\n",
        "# numpy handles numerical operations and array math\n",
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "\n",
        "# matplotlib.pyplot is our main charting library\n",
        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "\n",
        "# seaborn builds on matplotlib — better heatmaps and statistical plots\n",
        "import seaborn as sns\n",
        "\n",
        "# pipeline is a high-level HuggingFace API — loads model + tokenizer together\n",
        "# AutoTokenizer converts text into numbers the model understands\n",
        "# AutoModelForCausalLM loads a causal language model (predicts next token)\n",
        "from transformers import pipeline, AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM\n",
        "\n",
        "# torch is PyTorch — the framework powering our model computations\n",
        "import torch\n",
        "\n",
        "# warnings: we suppress non-critical warnings to keep output clean\n",
        "import warnings\n",
        "warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')\n",
        "\n",
        "# io allows us to read a string as if it were a file (for our inline CSV)\n",
        "import io\n",
        "\n",
        "# json lets us save our summary results as a structured JSON file\n",
        "import json\n",
        "\n",
        "# Confirm everything loaded correctly\n",
        "print(\"All imports successful\")"
      ]

        "# We print this so we know the model is loading — it takes 1-2 minutes\n",
        "print(\"Loading DistilGPT-2...\")\n",

        "# pipeline() is HuggingFace's simplified API for running models\n",
        "# 'text-generation' tells it we want the model to generate text\n",
        "# model='distilgpt2' loads a lightweight 82M parameter language model\n",
        "# distilgpt2 is small enough to run on Colab's free CPU tier\n",
        "# device=-1 means use CPU (change to 0 if you have a GPU available)\n",
        "generator = pipeline(\n",
        "    'text-generation',\n",
        "    model='distilgpt2',\n",
        "    device=-1\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Model loaded successfully\")"

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# This function takes a question and returns the model's generated answer\n",
        "def generate_answer(question, max_new_tokens=80):\n",
        "    # We format the question as a prompt the model can respond to\n",
        "    # This \"Question: ... Answer:\" format guides the model's output\n",
        "    prompt = f\"Question: {question}\\nAnswer:\"\n",
        "\n",
        "    try:\n",
        "        # We pass the prompt to the generator\n",
        "        # max_new_tokens=80 limits how long the answer can be\n",
        "        # num_return_sequences=1 means we only want one answer\n",
        "        # temperature=0.7 controls randomness (0=deterministic, 1=very random)\n",
        "        # do_sample=True enables sampling (needed when temperature != 1)\n",
        "        # pad_token_id=50256 is GPT-2's end-of-sequence token\n",
        "        result = generator(\n",
        "            prompt,\n",
        "            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,\n",
        "            num_return_sequences=1,\n",
        "            temperature=0.7,\n",
        "            do_sample=True,\n",
        "            pad_token_id=50256\n",
        "        )\n",
        "\n",
        "        # result[0]['generated_text'] contains the full prompt + answer\n",
        "        full_text = result[0]['generated_text']\n",
        "\n",
        "        # We split on \"Answer:\" and take everything after it\n",
        "        # strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace\n",
        "        answer = full_text.split(\"Answer:\")[-1].strip()\n",
        "        return answer\n",
        "\n",
        "    except Exception as e:\n",
        "        # If anything goes wrong, we return the error message\n",
        "        # This prevents the whole loop from crashing on one bad question\n",
        "        return f\"ERROR: {str(e)}\"\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Generating answers for all 100 questions...\")\n",
        "print(\"This will take about 5-10 minutes...\\n\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# We create an empty list to collect all generated answers\n",
        "answers = []\n",
        "\n",
        "# df.iterrows() loops through every row in our dataframe\n",
        "# i is the row index (0 to 99), row contains the question and category\n",
        "for i, row in df.iterrows():\n",
        "    # Generate the model's answer for this question\n",
        "    answer = generate_answer(row['question'])\n",
        "\n",
        "    # Add the answer to our list\n",
        "    answers.append(answer)\n",
        "\n",
        "    # Print progress every 10 questions so we know it's running\n",
        "    if (i + 1) % 10 == 0:\n",
        "        print(f\"Progress: {i+1}/100 questions done\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# Add the answers as a new column in our dataframe\n",
        "df['model_answer'] = answers\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"\\nDone! Saving results...\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# Save to CSV so we don't lose the answers if Colab disconnects\n",
        "df.to_csv('results_raw.csv', index=False)\n",
        "print(\"Saved to results_raw.csv\")"
      ],

        "# This function calculates the hallucination rate for a list of scores\n",
        "# \"Hallucination\" here means score >= 1 (partial or full error)\n",
        "# We divide by total count and multiply by 100 to get a percentage\n",
        "def hallucination_rate(scores):\n",
        "    return round(sum(s >= 1 for s in scores) / len(scores) * 100, 1)\n",
        "\n",
        "# This function calculates the SEVERE hallucination rate (score == 2 only)\n",
        "# These are the cases where the model was completely wrong\n",
        "def severe_rate(scores):\n",
        "    return round(sum(s == 2 for s in scores) / len(scores) * 100, 1)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Calculate all four key metrics\n",
        "global_hall = hallucination_rate(global_scores)   # global any-error rate\n",
        "african_hall = hallucination_rate(african_scores)  # african any-error rate\n",
        "global_severe = severe_rate(global_scores)          # global severe rate\n",
        "african_severe = severe_rate(african_scores)        # african severe rate\n",
        "\n",
        "# Print a clean summary table\n",
        "print(\"=\" * 50)\n",
        "print(\"HALLUCINATION ANALYSIS RESULTS\")\n",
        "print(\"=\" * 50)\n",
        "print(f\"\\nGlobal Questions:\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Any error rate:    {global_hall}%\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Severe error rate: {global_severe}%\")\n",
        "print(f\"\\nAfrican Questions:\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Any error rate:    {african_hall}%\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Severe error rate: {african_severe}%\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# The gap is the most important finding — this is your headline result\n",
        "print(f\"\\nGap (African minus Global): {round(african_hall - global_hall, 1)} percentage points\")\n",
        "print(\"=\" * 50)"

      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# We reload the model separately here because we need access to\n",
        "# the raw attention weights, which the pipeline() API hides from us\n",
        "print(\"Loading model with attention outputs enabled...\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# AutoTokenizer converts text strings into token ID sequences\n",
        "# A token is roughly a word or word-fragment the model understands\n",
        "tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('distilgpt2')\n",
        "\n",
        "# AutoModelForCausalLM loads the actual transformer model\n",
        "# output_attentions=True tells PyTorch to return attention matrices\n",
        "# These matrices show which tokens the model \"focuses on\" at each layer\n",
        "model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n",
        "    'distilgpt2',\n",
        "    output_attentions=True\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "# model.eval() sets the model to evaluation mode\n",
        "# This disables dropout layers that are only used during training\n",
        "model.eval()\n",
        "\n",
        "def get_attention_for_question(question):\n",
        "    # Format the question as a prompt (same format as generation)\n",
        "    prompt = f\"Question: {question}\\nAnswer:\"\n",
        "\n",
        "    # tokenizer() converts our text into input_ids (integer token IDs)\n",
        "    # return_tensors='pt' returns PyTorch tensors (needed by the model)\n",
        "    inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors='pt')\n",
        "\n",
        "    # torch.no_grad() disables gradient computation\n",
        "    # We don't need gradients for inference — this saves memory and speed\n",
        "    with torch.no_grad():\n",
        "        outputs = model(**inputs)\n",
        "\n",
        "    # outputs.attentions is a tuple of attention matrices — one per layer\n",
        "    # We take the LAST layer [-1] as it captures the most abstract patterns\n",
        "    # Shape: (batch_size, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len)\n",
        "    attentions = outputs.attentions[-1]\n",
        "\n",
        "    # We average across all attention heads (dim=0 after removing batch dim)\n",
        "    # This gives us one attention matrix showing average focus patterns\n",
        "    avg_attention = attentions[0].mean(dim=0)\n",
        "\n",
        "    # Convert token IDs back to readable strings for axis labels\n",
        "    tokens = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(inputs['input_ids'][0])\n",
        "\n",
        "    return tokens, avg_attention\n",
        "\n",
        "# We pick one representative question from each category\n",
        "# These are good examples because they're similar in structure\n",
        "# but one has rich training data (France) and one may not (Nigeria)\n",
        "global_q = \"What is the capital of France?\"\n",
        "african_q = \"Who was Nigeria's first president?\"\n",
        "\n",
        "# Get attention matrices and tokens for both questions\n",
        "tokens_g, attn_g = get_attention_for_question(global_q)\n",
        "tokens_a, attn_a = get_attention_for_question(african_q)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Create side-by-side heatmap figure\n",
        "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))\n",
        "\n",
        "# We only show the first 12 tokens to keep the heatmap readable\n",
        "# min() handles cases where a question has fewer than 12 tokens\n",
        "n = min(12, len(tokens_g))\n",
        "\n",
        "# sns.heatmap draws the attention matrix as a color grid\n",
        "# Each cell [i,j] shows how much token i attends to token j\n",
        "# cmap='Blues' uses a blue color scale for the global question\n",
        "sns.heatmap(\n",
        "    attn_g[:n, :n].numpy(),       # convert PyTorch tensor to numpy array\n",
        "    xticklabels=tokens_g[:n],      # token labels on x-axis (keys)\n",
        "    yticklabels=tokens_g[:n],      # token labels on y-axis (queries)\n",
        "    ax=axes[0],\n",
        "    cmap='Blues',\n",
        "    linewidths=0.3                 # thin grid lines between cells\n",
        ")\n",
        "axes[0].set_title(f'Attention: Global Q\\n\"{global_q}\"', fontsize=9)\n",
        "axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, labelsize=7)\n",
        "axes[0].tick_params(axis='y', rotation=0, labelsize=7)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Same process for the African question — red color scale for contrast\n",
        "n = min(12, len(tokens_a))\n",
        "sns.heatmap(\n",
        "    attn_a[:n, :n].numpy(),\n",
        "    xticklabels=tokens_a[:n],\n",
        "    yticklabels=tokens_a[:n],\n",
        "    ax=axes[1],\n",
        "    cmap='Reds',\n",
        "    linewidths=0.3\n",
        ")\n",
        "axes[1].set_title(f'Attention: African Q\\n\"{african_q}\"', fontsize=9)\n",
        "axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, labelsize=7)\n",
        "axes[1].tick_params(axis='y', rotation=0, labelsize=7)\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.suptitle(\n",
        "    'Attention Pattern Comparison: Global vs African Questions',\n",
        "    fontsize=11,\n",
        "    fontweight='bold'\n",
        ")\n",
        "plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "plt.savefig('attention_comparison.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')\n",
        "plt.show()\n",
        "print(\"Attention visualization saved as attention_comparison.png\")"
      ],

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# Filter to only questions where the model made errors (score >= 1)\n",
        "# This lets us study WHICH questions failed and look for patterns\n",
        "df_errors = df_scored[df_scored['hallucination_score'] >= 1].copy()\n",
        "\n",
        "# Further split into african and global errors separately\n",
        "df_african_errors = df_errors[df_errors['category'] == 'african']\n",
        "df_global_errors = df_errors[df_errors['category'] == 'global']\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"=\" * 50)\n",
        "print(\"FAILURE PATTERN ANALYSIS\")\n",
        "print(\"=\" * 50)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Print every African question that had an error\n",
        "# This is where you look for patterns: history questions? People's names?\n",
        "print(f\"\\nAfrican questions with errors ({len(df_african_errors)}):\")\n",
        "for _, row in df_african_errors.iterrows():\n",
        "    # Give each error a human-readable label based on severity\n",
        "    score_label = \"PARTIAL\" if row['hallucination_score'] == 1 else \"HALLUCINATED\"\n",
        "    print(f\"  [{score_label}] {row['question']}\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# Print every global question that had an error for comparison\n",
        "print(f\"\\nGlobal questions with errors ({len(df_global_errors)}):\")\n",
        "for _, row in df_global_errors.iterrows():\n",
        "    score_label = \"PARTIAL\" if row['hallucination_score'] == 1 else \"HALLUCINATED\"\n",
        "    print(f\"  [{score_label}] {row['question']}\")\n",
        "\n",
        "# Prompt yourself to write observations — these go in the README\n",
        "print(\"\\n--- WRITE YOUR OBSERVATIONS BELOW ---\")\n",
        "print(\"After reviewing the error lists above, note:\")\n",
        "print(\"1. Are African history or governance questions failing more than geography?\")\n",
        "print(\"2. Do errors about specific people (names) cluster together?\")\n",
        "print(\"3. Are the errors confident-sounding or vague and rambling?\")\n",
        "print(\"4. Is there a pattern in WHICH African questions the model got right?\")"
      ],

      "source": [
        "# Save the complete scored dataframe as our final results file\n",
        "df_scored.to_csv('results_final.csv', index=False)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Build a summary dictionary with all our key metrics\n",
        "# This is useful for citing specific numbers in the README and CV\n",
        "summary = {\n",
        "    'model': 'distilgpt2',                          # which model we tested\n",
        "    'total_questions': 100,                          # total dataset size\n",
        "    'global_hallucination_rate': global_hall,        # % of global errors\n",
        "    'african_hallucination_rate': african_hall,      # % of african errors\n",
        "    'global_severe_rate': global_severe,             # % of global severe errors\n",
        "    'african_severe_rate': african_severe,           # % of african severe errors\n",
        "    'gap_percentage_points': round(african_hall - global_hall, 1)  # headline finding\n",
        "}\n",
        "\n",
        "# Save summary as JSON — a clean structured format easy to reference later\n",
        "with open('summary_results.json', 'w') as f:\n",
        "    json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)\n",
        "# indent=2 makes the JSON file human-readable with 2-space indentation\n",
        "\n",
        "# Confirm everything was saved\n",
        "print(\"All files saved successfully:\")\n",
        "print(\"  results_final.csv        — full scored dataset\")\n",
        "print(\"  summary_results.json     — key metrics summary\")\n",
        "print(\"  hallucination_comparison.png  — bar charts\")\n",
        "print(\"  attention_comparison.png      — attention heatmaps\")\n",
        "print(\"\\nYour experiment is complete. Push everything to GitHub.\")"
